executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with documented human spillover risk, a resurgent dengue epidemic, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with RSV co-circulation. Mpox continues to spread in the Americas region, while pertussis is experiencing a notable resurgence across multiple countries. The simultaneous circulation of multiple respiratory pathogens and vector-borne diseases creates compounded public health burden requiring coordinated multinational response.
bottomLine: Multiple concurrent epidemic threats—led by H5N1, dengue, mpox, and a resurgent pertussis wave—are straining public health systems across the Americas and Europe simultaneously as the Southern Hemisphere influenza season begins.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained activity
Continued animal-to-human spillover risk with zoonotic transmission documented across the region
Repeated alerts suggest expanding geographic spread beyond initial foci
threats.action: Enhance surveillance at human-animal interface, enforce biosafety at poultry and livestock operations, pre-position antiviral stockpiles, and activate pandemic preparedness protocols

threats.name: Dengue
signals: Epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating elevated case counts
Historical pattern of early-year surge consistent with peak transmission season
Broad regional circulation across multiple PAHO member states
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations, activate case management surge capacity, issue travel health advisories, and accelerate dengue vaccination where licensed

threats.name: Mpox
signals: Dedicated epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission
Sustained community spread beyond initial outbreak clusters
Regional alert maintained indicating no evidence of containment
threats.action: Expand ring vaccination with MVA-BN vaccine, strengthen contact tracing infrastructure, and enhance laboratory diagnostic capacity across the region

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating persistent and worsening transmission
Resurgence pattern suggests waning population immunity and possible vaccine hesitancy
Multi-month sustained alert period reflects failure of initial control measures
threats.action: Boost childhood vaccination coverage, implement Tdap catch-up campaigns for adolescents and adults, and prioritize vaccination of pregnant women and healthcare workers

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
signals: PAHO alert issued April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
January 2026 alert documented simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation stressing healthcare systems
December 2025 alert flagged Northern Hemisphere season onset creating year-round global burden
threats.action: Accelerate influenza vaccination for high-risk groups, ensure RSV prophylaxis availability for infants and elderly, and prepare hospital surge capacity

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: Epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active cases or heightened risk
Ongoing enzootic activity in jungle zones with human exposure risk
Alert level suggests cases beyond expected baseline
threats.action: Enforce mandatory vaccination for travelers to endemic zones, conduct emergency vaccination campaigns in at-risk communities, and strengthen entomological surveillance

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Co-circulation with dengue in same Aedes-endemic regions amplifying vector control challenges
Alert timing suggests early seasonal surge
threats.action: Strengthen integrated Aedes vector control, enhance clinical surveillance to differentiate from dengue, and issue public awareness campaigns

threats.name: Measles
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating cases in a region previously nearing elimination
Likely linked to pandemic-era vaccination coverage gaps and imported cases
Continued ECDC weekly threat reporting suggests European importation risk as well
threats.action: Conduct urgent MMR vaccination catch-up campaigns targeting under-vaccinated communities, strengthen airport and port-of-entry surveillance, and ensure outbreak response teams are on standby

diseases: Communicable disease threats (ECDC weekly monitoring - multiple pathogens)

amrSignals: Repeated Bordetella pertussis resurgence despite vaccination may warrant investigation into vaccine-escape strains or altered pathogen fitness
Sustained multi-month transmission of pertussis across the Americas despite existing immunization programs suggests possible reduced vaccine effectiveness or emerging resistance to immune pressure
GLP-1 receptor agonist misuse alert (Report 12) indirectly signals pharmaceutical supply chain vulnerabilities that may affect antimicrobial access and distribution
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen epidemic pressure across the Americas in early 2026 suggests compounded healthcare system stress with limited surge capacity
Dual PAHO alerts for both Southern Hemisphere influenza season start (April 2026) and Northern Hemisphere season (December 2025) indicate near year-round influenza burden globally
Repeated issuance of pertussis updates over a 4-month period (December 2025 to March 2026) signals failure of initial public health interventions and possible endemic re-establishment
Co-circulation of multiple Aedes-transmitted arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in the same geographic zones creates diagnostic confusion and overwhelms vector control resources
H5N1 persistence in the Americas across two consecutive PAHO update cycles suggests entrenched animal reservoir activity with escalating pandemic risk

ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly threat reports through April–May 2026 reflects sustained elevated European disease activity likely driven by imported cases from the Americas and endemic resurgences
